content_units: Ontario Leak-Repair Prep Checklist

Before contacting the landlord again, the tenant should organize a clear, dated repair file focused on   what happened, when, how bad it is, and what access is needed  . In Ontario, the most useful prep is practical: a tidy evidence package, a short repair request, and a log showing the issue is repeated and worsening.
Repeated Leak Documentation Checklist
Item   What to prepare   Why it helps   Status
Incident timeline   Note leaks on   2026-01-10  ,   2026-01-22  , and   2026-02-03   with time noticed, room, and where water entered   Shows this is recurring, not a one-off   Ready to compile

Photos and videos   Gather all photos already taken; add new wide shots and close-ups of ceiling/wall/closet areas, water staining, damp items, and any visible mold-like growth   Makes damage progression easy to see   Partly ready
Prior communications   Save the two emails already sent, including sent dates, subject lines, attachments, and any landlord replies or no-response gaps   Proves notice was already given   Ready

Damage notes   List affected areas: apartment room(s), bedroom closet, odor, damaged belongings, damp drywall/paint, recurring drip or stain pattern   Helps landlord understand scope and urgency   Needs update

Mold-smell record   Write down when the   mold smell started  , how often it is noticeable, and whether the closet contents feel damp   Flags possible habitability/health concern without overstating   Needs update
Access readiness   Prepare 2-3 date/time windows when workers can enter and note any entry instructions   Removes delay excuses and speeds scheduling   Needs update
Repair request message   Draft one concise email requesting inspection and repair of the recurring leak and moisture source   Keeps the ask specific and professional   Needs draft
What to Include in the Repair Request
Use one short email or letter with these points:
- State that there have been   repeated water leaks   on   Jan 10, Jan 22, and Feb 3, 2026  .
- Say that   photos were emailed twice already  .
- Identify the affected area clearly, including the   bedroom closet  .
- Mention that a   mold smell is starting  .
- Ask for:
- inspection of the leak source
- repair of the underlying cause, not just cosmetic patching
- assessment of moisture-damaged areas
- confirmation of when maintenance will attend
- Offer reasonable entry availability.
- Ask for a written response and repair timeline.
A practical subject line:
-   Request for repair – repeated water leaks and mold odor
Tenant Prep Notes for a Strong Paper Trail
- Keep everything in   one folder  : photos, videos, emails, notes, and any receipts.
- Rename files by date, such as:
- `2026-01-10-bedroom-ceiling-leak-1.jpg`
- `2026-02-03-closet-water-stain.jpg`
- Start a simple running log with:
- date
- what was observed
- odor level
- new damage
- whether landlord/super was contacted
- If belongings were affected, make a separate list with:
- item
- location
- type of damage
- estimated value or receipt if available
- If safe to do so, note whether the area feels damp, paint is bubbling, or drywall is soft.
- Avoid making repairs that could hide evidence before the landlord inspects, except reasonable steps to protect property.
Ready-to-Send Checklist
Option 1: Evidence bundle   Timeline + photos + prior emails in one package   Best for a clear first repair request
Organize Files
Option 2: Concise written notice   One email with dates, affected area, smell, and access times   Best for fast landlord follow-up
Send Request
Option 3: Ongoing condition log   Daily notes if leak/moisture continues after notice   Best if the issue worsens or repeats again
Track Updates
Option 4: Health-and-safety detail sheet   Record mold odor, damp closet contents, and any sensitivity symptoms factually   Useful if urgency increases
Review Tenant Help
